page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the N2 family. It is equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, utilizing hyperthreading with 2 threads per core. The instance features 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities across most standard operations. The instance achieves average ratings in multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng, Passmark CPU testing, and Geekbench software compilation. Memory bandwidth is measured at 413.79 GB/sec for cached read-only small blocks and approximately 50.27 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, certain workloads show limitations, with weak performance observed in single-core stress-ng tests, Geekbench multi-core scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

This instance is suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 6.9 GB/sec, and database operations, supported by a Redis SET performance of 7.12 million operations per second. It is also capable of handling lightweight text processing and small-scale software compilation. Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced resource profile, it offers a stable, predictable option for standard business applications without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or compute-optimized hardware.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.8 GHz. The hardware features 4 physical cores with hyperthreading, a 33 MB L3 cache, and lacks bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark data positions this instance in the average tier for multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and static web serving throughput, though it exhibits weaker single-core and multi-threaded decompression capabilities. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for balanced workloads, offering predictable resource allocation. The n2-standard-8 is best suited for general-purpose applications, including static web serving, standard database operations, and moderate software compilation tasks.
